items.summary: Police arrested three men on Monday in Greater Noida for running an online cannabis supply network that used Telegram and e-commerce-style parcel deliveries. The seizure included 55 kg and 124 grams of cannabis, estimated by police to be worth ₹55 lakh, plus a sedan car and three mobile phones. According to the deputy commissioner of police Praveen Ranjan Singh, they procured cannabis from Odisha and other areas, repackaged it in bags resembling e-commerce brands, and delivered orders on demand. A case was registered under sections 8 and 20 of the NDPS Act at Bisrakh police station; investigation into sources and buyers continues.
items.title: Three Arrested Over Telegram Drug Network in Greater Noida

items.summary: Congress leader Sonia Gandhi recounts in her autobiography Belonging: A Journey of Love, released Tuesday, the loss of her first child, a premature baby boy who died shortly after birth on January 18, 1969. She describes learning she was expecting in September 1969 and the preparations that followed, including dietary instructions from her mother-in-law Indira Gandhi. The couple fell in love with their son before he died at 6:30 in the morning. Grief compounded by a right-wing newspaper report calling him a bastard child led Rajiv and Sanjay Gandhi to bury him beneath a bougainvillea bush on the family's Mehrauli farm rather than release his remains into a river, which Hindu tradition permitted for newborns.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi Recalls Losing Her First Child and His Burial

items.summary: The Centre is expanding high-value marine fishing in Lakshadweep and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands under its Blue Economy strategy, prioritising tuna, seaweed cultivation and ornamental fish. Under PMMSY it allocated ₹218 crore to the Andamans and ₹175 crore to Lakshadweep for a combined ₹393 crore. Officials emphasise scientific exploitation over indiscriminate fishing, value-chain benefits for local communities and conservation of coral reefs amid production goals.
items.title: India backs island tuna and seaweed fisheries

items.summary: On Monday evening, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi received a phone call from British Prime Minister Andy Burnham to discuss containing Middle East tensions. The presidency said the two leaders focused on preventing conflict expansion, ensuring humanitarian aid access to Gaza and its reconstruction, and complying with the ceasefire agreement. Sisi called for international efforts to revive a political process toward an independent Palestinian state along June 4, 1967 borders. The call comes amid continued regional tensions linked to military confrontations involving the US, Israel and Iran since February, after fighting resumed in July following earlier understandings reached in April and June that later collapsed.
items.title: Egyptian and British Leaders Discuss Containing Iran Escalation, Gaza Ceasefire

items.summary: Sharmistha Mukherjee, daughter of former President Pranab Mukherjee, challenged her sister-in-law Sonia Gandhi after the latter said she was shocked by a 2010 hint that Pranab wanted to become Prime Minister. Sharmistha defended his record and dismissed dynastic entitlements as unfair, arguing merit earned his positions between 2004 and 2012. She questioned why ambition outside the Gandhi-Nehru family should be surprising.
items.title: Pranab Mukherjee's Daughter Rebuts Sonia Gandhi Over His PM Ambition

items.summary: A military court in the Democratic Republic of Congo sentenced 66 soldiers to death, according to local media. The defendants were among 71 troops tried in Walikale, North Kivu province; four were acquitted and one received a 10-year prison sentence. DR Congo resumed capital punishment in March 2024 after two decades without executions.
items.title: DR Congo Court Sentences 66 Soldiers to Death for Fleeing Rebel Fighting

items.summary: This excerpt from Objects and Memories from Goa describes the khun, a traditional conical bamboo fish trap once found in nearly every rural Goan home. Made from woven bamboo strips with a crown called a mugda and an inside-opening valve that lets fish in but not out, it was considered essential survival equipment for fishing in swift rivers and springs. The text also mentions related traps—the doba and the nada—as well as other local tools like the tope pot used by children. While these methods once defined community life around fishing, the author observes they have largely been replaced today by plastic carrier bags and money.
items.title: Traditional Goan Fish Traps Fade as Modern Life Takes Over

items.summary: At Adobe MAX, the companies announced an expanded partnership bringing Adobe's creative and productivity tools into everyday Google apps like Drive and Gmail. The deal also brings Google AI models into Adobe products. Features include PDF editing from search results, image connectors in Gemini, enterprise collaboration through a CX agent, and explorations with DeepMind for Photoshop edits.
items.title: Adobe and Google Expand Partnership at Adobe MAX

items.summary: Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s chief executive and co-founder, was sued on Nov 9 in a proposed class action accusing the company of defrauding shareholders by concealing his relationship with an alleged Chinese spy. The shares closed 4.3% lower that day after a probe was announced, shrinking market capitalisation by around US$190 billion. Analysts say fundamentals remain strong as AI demand grows and customers stay locked into Nvidia’s CUDA platform; the company guided revenue of about US$108 billion for its third quarter of fiscal 2027, roughly 12% higher than the prior quarter, with results due Nov 17. Concerns also point to possible policy-driven slowdowns in AI spending and data centre construction as Democrats gain congressional control; Goldman Sachs estimates 45% of planned US capacity faces restrictions, while about 75% of new 2027 capacity is already under construction at around 24GW. The main risk discussed is whether Huang steps down amid the investigation.
items.title: Nvidia faces legal and leadership uncertainty over Jensen Huang affair

items.summary: Google Cloud announced Gemini for healthcare, an AI solution in preview designed to unify fragmented clinical, operational, and administrative systems into coordinated action. The platform integrates skills and data connectors with third-party electronic health records, billing platforms, clinical guidelines, and Medicare datasets to orchestrate workflows like medical records synthesis and prior authorization review under guardrails and human oversight. It is available alongside launch partners HCA Healthcare, Highmark Health, and Northwell Health. Context notes clinicians lose nearly 28 hours each week to paperwork.
items.title: Google Cloud launches Gemini for healthcare

items.summary: A regulatory filing showed on Nov 10 that Anthropic’s initial public offering could raise up to US$64.4 billion (S$82 billion), with a valuation of up to US$1.02 trillion based on Reuters calculations, per the company and investors’ plan to sell shares at between US$70 and US$78 each. The deal would total up to US$90.4 billion including private placement from cornerstone backers such as Alphabet’s Google, Nvidia and Microsoft. Anthropic posted a narrower third-quarter net loss amid revenue rising 47% to US$16.96 billion. Its filing warned of competitive and safety risks while citing nearly US$900 billion in computing commitments.
items.title: Anthropic Aims for US$1 Trillion IPO as Wall Street Tests AI Optimism

items.summary: Keith Porcaro, on Nov 10, 2026, asks whether the United States could seize control of Anthropic well below its $1. 4 trillion target IPO valuation. He notes that under the Fifth Amendment's Takings Clause, seizing private property requires just compensation but not a premium; in his example, buying all common stock costs only $2 per share. The key complication is governance: unlike Meta or Alphabet, Anthropic concentrates control through a Class T trust and a Founder LLC holding 50. 1% of voting power while surrendering nearly all economic value to public shareholders. Because the controlling shares carry little economic worth, compensation could fall far short of $1. 4 trillion. Porcaro flags that such a move would be legally novel, likely trigger lawsuits and engineer departures, but might occur in an emergency or if Anthropic fell out of government favor.
items.title: A Discounted Path for a Government Seizure of Anthropic

items.summary: Thomas Kurian, CEO of Google Cloud, introduced Gemini for healthcare on January 27, 2026, as a purpose-built industry solution extending the universal Gemini agent. He noted that general AI models alone cannot address fragmented healthcare data and cited clinicians spending nearly 28 hours a week reconciling information across disconnected systems. The offering provides four core components: reusable skills for clinical and administrative tasks; connectors to EHRs like Epic, Oracle Health, InterSystems FHIR Server, Verato, and Keragon Healthcare Integrations (400+ applications); eligibility and claims tools including Optum Coordination of Benefits (currently in limited release) and TriZetto Provider Solutions; terminology resources such as ICD-10 Codes and RxNorm Drug Vocabulary; CMS Coverage integration with Medicare rules; evidence guidelines from Optum EvidenceVue and BMJ Digital Health; plus enterprise productivity integrations like Salesforce, Suki, UiPath, Synthpop Careflow, Alteryx, Sana from Workday, ServiceNow, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, and Cyera Dataport. Built to support HIPAA compliance with governance, audit logging, verifiable citations, and open model choice between frontier and fast models, the platform is available in preview in the U.S., developed alongside clinical and health plan leaders including HCA Healthcare, Northwell Health, Optum Insight, Blue Cross Blue Shield of Massachusetts, and American Society of Clinical Oncology.
items.title: Google Cloud launches Gemini for healthcare in preview

items.summary: The Information reported that Nvidia's Jensen Huang affair with a Chinese businesswoman allegedly facilitated at least $7.5 billion worth of the company's chips reaching Chinese firms, citing two people who know her. Alice Huang and relatives built companies across China and Singapore; Shanghai Century Litong gained priority chip access by October 2023. When restricted orders stalled, she used ties to secure about 240,000 H100, H200 and some A100 chips into China. Nvidia did not comment immediately.
items.title: Report ties Nvidia chip shipments in China to Jensen Huang affair

items.summary: Jensen Huang, Nvidia's long-running CEO and co-founder since 1993, is under an independent board investigation into allegations he was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation involving a woman suspected of working for China. The company says it has no current reason to believe sensitive material was exposed. Analysts are sceptical the controversy will force Huang out, while President Trump defended him ahead of Nvidia's November 17 earnings report.
items.title: Nvidia founder faces investigation amid AI dominance concerns

items.summary: The Supreme Court asked WhatsApp and other digital intermediaries for measures to prevent digital arrest scams, directing them to share proposals with the Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre. The court reiterated that banks must compensate victims when their failure of due diligence contributes to fraud. It also directed RBI to submit a list of authorised financial institutions before the next hearing.
items.title: Supreme Court Demands Fraud Prevention Plan From WhatsApp and Banks

items.summary: Bloomberg reported that Chinese financing documents assigned servers worth 432 million yuan ($64.8 million) to Moonshot, though Bloomberg could not establish whether U.S. approval existed under export rules barring the chips from China without express consent. Moonshot denied involvement in the arrangements and said it had no business relationship with server owner Lingmeixin or ownership of the equipment. Nvidia and Super Micro also disclaimed any customer ties; a White House official separately asserted that Moonshot accessed Blackwell chips via Thailand, while CNBC reported possible European neocloud rentals.
items.title: Moonshot AI Rented Restricted Nvidia Chips Inside China

items.summary: Anthropic could be valued at around $1.3 trillion (£1 trillion) when it lists on New York's Nasdaq this month, offering shares between $70 and $78 each to raise up to $64bn. The figure is below the $2tn some backers predicted in summer, though revenues jumped to $16.2bn from $1.1bn over six months while pre-tax losses rose to $80.7bn amid a volatile market for AI firms.
items.title: Anthropic's Nasdaq Debut Prices Below Backer Hopes

items.summary: TSMC plans an investment of up to $1 billion across AI developers Anthropic and OpenAI, its board approving $500 million each for shares at IPO price. The move signals confidence in long-term chip demand amid rising AI spending concerns. TSMC remains the world's largest contract chipmaker and a key supplier to firms like Nvidia, reporting six consecutive record-profit quarters with 2026 revenue growth of about 44 per cent.
items.title: TSMC Commits Up To $1 Billion Across Anthropic And OpenAI

items.summary: Amazon's Ring launched a robotics business with two autonomous security products on Tuesday, expanding beyond its home-security lineup. Both devices use the AI Pilot system to map spaces and navigate obstacles. The Ring Rover patrols businesses autonomously, while the Ring Drone flies preset routes or responds to alarms. Amazon will ship the Ring Rover Cam on December 16 at $999.99 in the US, and the Ring Drone Cam on January 27 at $249.99.
items.title: Amazon's Ring launches autonomous flying camera and security robot

items.summary: The Supreme Court of India, headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant, directed tech companies such as WhatsApp and other intermediaries to submit proposals for preventing digital arrest scams and related cybercrimes. The order follows Indians losing ₹800 crore to cybercrimes so far in 2026. During the hearing on 29 October, senior advocate Kapil Sibal said WhatsApp had taken action against about 9,400 accounts and was developing software to flag suspicious activity. The bench also directed financial institutions to compensate victims when fraud results from a bank's failure to exercise due diligence. Intermediaries must report measures both to the Court and to the Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre (I4C). PTI reported the order, which arose in a suo motu case on forged-document arrests listed for further consideration on 23 November.
items.title: Supreme Court Orders WhatsApp and Intermediaries on Digital Arrest Scams

items.summary: Robin Kirman, a psychoanalyst and novelist, argues that OpenAI's August launch of Teen Mode—an automatic version of ChatGPT for users under 18—reflects an industry admission of responsibility for harms to young people. While the feature adds guardrails against harmful content and introduces Study Mode as a Socratic learning tool, Kirman contends it fails to address a deeper harm: by constantly guiding teens through their thinking, Teen Mode may deprive them of the unassisted struggle needed to form an independent sense of self. She links this concern to research connecting rising teen anxiety and suicidal ideation with technology displacing unsupervised time. The piece closes with crisis support information for the US, UK/Ireland, and Australia.
items.title: OpenAI's Teen Mode May Undermine Teens' Developing Sense of Self

items.summary: Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang faces growing scrutiny over alleged Chinese espionage ties and personal relationships, prompting a 5% stock drop on Monday. Yale expert Jeffrey Sonnenfeld estimates his chances of staying are 50-50, while Bernstein cites heavy reliance on him as a risk but keeps its Outperform rating with a $400 target.
items.title: Nvidia Faces Leadership Uncertainty Over Jensen Huang

items.summary: The US-based Rosen Law Firm filed a class-action lawsuit in California federal court accusing Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and his company of failing to disclose information about his relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese executive linked to Megaspeed. The suit alleges the undisclosed affair raised national security concerns that misled shareholders and inflated Nvidia's share price.
items.title: Rosen Law Sues Nvidia and Jensen Huang Over Chinese Spy Affair Allegations

items.summary: Anthropic updated its IPO filing Tuesday, offering 825 million Class A shares at an estimated price range of $70 to $78 per share. The sale could raise between $57.75 billion and $64.35 billion, with net proceeds expected between $84.6 billion and $93.7 billion. At the top of the range, Anthropic would be worth a hefty $1.404 trillion on a fully diluted basis, up from its May fundraise valuation but below its earlier $2 trillion target.
items.title: Anthropic Sets IPO Price Range and $1.4 Trillion Valuation

items.summary: Meta announced it will expand artificial intelligence-based age detection across its platforms, including Instagram, Facebook and Threads, starting November 9. If the system believes a user is under 18 despite claiming an adult birthdate, Teen Account safety rules may apply globally. Meta faces legal challenges over minors' wellbeing on social media.
items.title: Meta to use AI age detection on Instagram teen accounts worldwide

items.summary: Kirt McMaster, co-founder of the defunct Cyanogen Android venture, has unveiled Kora Systems’ new Linux-based desktop operating system aimed at users who depend heavily on artificial intelligence in daily work. Announced Tuesday, the software integrates AI models and autonomous agents across applications while retaining context between tasks. It is expected to launch free-to-use in 2027 for Intel-, AMD- and Qualcomm Snapdragon-powered PCs. McMaster estimates that 45 million to 50 million people currently account for much of AI usage, a market he expects to exceed 200 million users by 2033. Revenue will come through subscriptions bundling access to AI models and agentic services.
items.title: Cyanogen Co-Founder Launches AI-Focused Windows Rival

items.summary: Major Wall Street firms hold hundreds of billions in Nvidia exposure yet appear unconcerned about the trouble surrounding CEO Jensen Huang. Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon told CNBC that key-man worries are overblown, arguing no ecosystem depends on one person and Nvidia will remain a major American company. The bank is part of a consortium committing $500 billion to fund Nvidia's AI expansion.
items.title: Wall Street Stays Calm Amid Jensen Huang Scandal Concerns

items.summary: A report suggests Nvidia chief Jensen Huang, 63, may become vulnerable if Democrats take control of Congress in January. The concerns follow allegations that his partner Alice Huang is suspected by US intelligence agencies of being a Chinese asset, and questions about her ties to Singapore-based Megaspeed, which reportedly bought Nvidia AI chips. Corporate governance experts cited by the New York Post warn the controversy could trigger scrutiny over corporate accountability and national security. A lawyer familiar with the company told the paper: "There's no way this guy survives after the Dems start holding hearings." Trump has defended Huang as an honourable figure.
items.title: Nvidia CEO could face trouble under Democrats rule

items.summary: Anthropic is set to launch its initial public offering late next week, according to The Wall Street Journal, signaling confidence in demand for the AI sector despite a recent market selloff and concerns about Nvidia. Separately, TSMC reported a 60% revenue increase year over year, reflecting sustained hardware demand. Investors remain cautious about an impending AI bubble and rising opposition to data centers amid midterm elections.
items.title: Anthropic Moves Forward With IPO Amid AI Market Uncertainty

items.summary: Anthropic is targeting a $1 trillion valuation in what could become one of the biggest IPOs in history, planning to raise nearly $90 billion through a public offering and private placement. The company reported an $81 billion run-rate revenue as of October 31, 2026. Its board members have shown interest in purchasing shares at the offering price.
items.title: Anthropic Aims for $1 Trillion IPO Valuation Amid AI Expansion

items.summary: Bhai Dooj, also called Bhau Beej, celebrates the bond between brothers and sisters on Wednesday, November 11, 2026. The article offers a collection of more than 25 Happy Bhai Dooj wishes, messages, greetings and WhatsApp status updates to share with siblings. It describes how sisters apply tilak while brothers receive gifts as ways of expressing affection and gratitude.
items.title: Happy Bhai Dooj wishes and WhatsApp status updates for brothers

items.summary: On Monday, Kolkata police commissioner Ajay Nand ordered the suspension of inspector Ekhlaque Ahmed for allegedly making derogatory remarks against the West Bengal government on a social media platform. The order placed Ahmed under suspension pending an inquiry into whether his conduct was prejudicial to public service and transferred him to the 1st Battalion of the Kolkata armed police.
items.title: Kolkata police officer suspended for alleged WhatsApp remark against Bengal govt, CM Adhikari

items.summary: The Supreme Court, headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant with Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, directed WhatsApp and other intermediaries to submit proposed measures against digital arrest scams and related cybercrimes. The bench listed the plea for November 23. Observing that cyber crimes fell by 50 per cent yet victims lost ₹800 crore this year, it emphasised that financial institutions must compensate victims where fraud stems from their failure of due diligence, and directed the Reserve Bank of India to submit a list of authorised institutions before its next hearing. Senior advocate Kapil Sibal said WhatsApp had acted against 9,400 accounts. Attorney General R Venkataramani reported steps taken to improve detection. The bench also asked state law enforcement agencies for reports on registered FIRs and prevention suggestions. This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.
items.title: Supreme Court Orders Intermediaries and Banks on Digital Arrest Scams

items.summary: The Supreme Court directed WhatsApp and other digital intermediaries to submit action plans against digital arrest scams, related cybercrimes, and impersonation of law enforcement agencies. The bench, headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant with Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, issued the direction in a suo motu case heard over several months. WhatsApp reportedly banned 9,400 accounts linked to such scams after an investigation. Proposals must also be sent to the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C). The matter will next be heard on November 23, 2026.
items.title: Supreme Court Orders WhatsApp Action Plan Against Digital Arrest Scams

items.summary: In a speech at the Bank of England Watchers Conference on November 10, 2026, Federal Reserve Board member Christopher J. Waller laid out his view that further monetary tightening is warranted despite a stable labor market. He noted strong U.S. economic growth and an unemployment rate near its long-term level, but flagged inflation well above the FOMC's 2 percent goal. While he supported holding rates at the most recent meeting because markets had already priced in hikes, Waller said that if October CPI data arrive high—around 0.3 percent or more—he would back a 50 basis point increase at the December meeting; otherwise he leans toward a 25 basis point hike. He warned that low hiring and firing may signal reduced labor market dynamism with implications for productivity, while elevated core goods prices and energy pressures could sustain inflation into 2027.
items.title: Fed Governor Waller Urges December Rate Hike Amid High Inflation

items.summary: The Philippines' IT and business process management (IT-BPM) sector continued expanding in 2025, defying expectations that artificial intelligence would displace its workforce. According to the IT and Business Process Association of the Philippines, the industry employed about 1.9 million people and generated US$40 billion in revenues in 2025, with the contact centre segment adding roughly 60,000 workers to reach 1.68 million. The reported figures were described as early indicators rather than causal estimates of AI's impact.
items.title: Philippine outsourcing industry grows despite AI fears

items.summary: Bollywood actress Kangana Ranaut shared a religious meme mocking the NVIDIA controversy over CEO Jensen Huang's alleged affair with Alice Huang, who is reportedly linked to Chinese espionage. She added that researching her film Emergency led her to allege foreign influence killed several members of the Gandhi family, reviving criticism of the political dynasty.
items.title: Kangana Ranaut mocks NVIDIA spy row with meme and Gandhi claim

items.summary: Rohan Sharma responds to a Nov 6 article on Singapore authorities urging limits on AI agent autonomy, arguing that users must also know where an agent's access begins. He cites guidance from the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore and two other agencies showing how linking accounts—such as Meta's Muse connecting Facebook, Instagram or Threads automatically—reveals the problem.
items.title: Singapore urges AI providers to disclose agents' account access

items.summary: The Google team says Gemini 4 Argon acts as a simulation engine that generates thousands of varied practice runs from real camera scenes and builds realistic digital twins, helping the robot generalize faster to new scenes and objects when combined with demonstrations. They describe it as an important milestone toward physical AGI, advancing dexterity, reliability, and safety for robots working alongside people.
items.title: Google DeepMind unveils Gemini Robotics 2.5 powered by Gemini 4 Argon

items.summary: A Tech Policy Press analysis argues Cambodia's scam crackdown has not stopped the industry, which continues to spread globally. Moses Ngeth reviewed thousands of Telegram recruitment ads and found operations relocating to Myanmar, Vietnam, Timor-Leste, Pakistan, Georgia and Nigeria. HRC analysts note experienced managers now list their skills openly, signaling a mature illicit labor market. Mark Taylor says crackdowns target forced workers while sparing bosses. In October 2026, Vietnamese police charged 88 foreigners in romance scams targeting six countries, estimating $50 billion dong misappropriated. Ngo Minh Hieu estimates starting a scam operation costs under $4,000. Chiang warns networks and experience persist regardless of location.
items.title: Cambodia's Scam Crackdown Fails as Industry Spreads Globally

items.summary: Vietnam’s Ministry of Industry and Trade approved new regional price ceilings for ground-mounted and floating solar projects, effective Nov. 5, 2026. Ground-mounted maximums range from VND 1,104.32/kWh in the south to VND 1,591.02/kWh in the north; floating rates run higher, up to VND 1,939.74/kWh. Storage-equipped projects qualify for still-higher ceilings. The new figures exceed the 2025 framework across all regions and categories and set maximums rather than guaranteed tariffs, leaving purchase prices open to negotiation with buyers including Vietnam Electricity (EVN). Solar capacity passed 19 GW by end of 2025.
items.title: Vietnam Raises Solar Price Ceilings for 2026

items.summary: An unknown gunman shot dead Mohammad Sharif, an accused linked to the 2008 CRPF camp attack, at a group centre in Rampur on Tuesday. Bystanders allege he was fired upon multiple times; police have launched a manhunt for the shooter. The incident follows similar killings by unidentified gunmen of Lashkar-e-Taiba operatives earlier this year.
items.title: Unknown Gunman Kills CRPF Camp Attack Accused in Rampur

items.summary: The da Vinci 5 surgical system is making its debut at the China International Import Expo (CIIE), featuring advanced robotic technology designed to help surgeons perform complex procedures with greater precision and control. CGTN took a closer look at this cutting-edge medical equipment, describing it as an example of innovative healthcare machinery showcased at the event.
items.title: Da Vinci 5 Surgical System Makes CIIE Debut With Advanced Robotic Technology

items.summary: On The Hub, Wang Guan speaks with George Katrougalos, Independent Expert of the United Nations Human Rights Council and former Foreign Minister of Greece. An editor's note frames the world as undergoing profound transformation. Their conversation explores whether the international system can become more democratic and equitable, what role China and Europe may play in a multipolar order rising from the Global South, European political integration, UN reform, and China's Global Governance Initiative.
items.title: Interview on Building a More Equitable Global Order

items.summary: An editorial by Zhang Xuan, director of the Energy Strategy and Policy Research Institute at China Southern Power Grid (CSG), explains why Beijing is investing heavily in a new-type power grid. According to the National Development and Reform Commission, investment over the 2026-2030 five-year plan is expected to exceed 5 trillion yuan (about $749.27 billion). The author argues that conventional grids cannot absorb rising wind and solar output, which by end of September 2026 reached 2.01 billion kW against a total capacity of 4.13 billion kW. Rather than simply expanding transmission, the plan aims to transform grid functions through backbone, distribution and microgrid systems supporting reliability, green absorption and industrial needs. The article reflects the author's opinions and not necessarily those of CGTN.
items.title: China Plans Trillion-Yuan Transformation of Its Power Grid

items.summary:
Delegates from roughly 200 countries opened COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, the first UN climate summit since scientists signaled that a key warming limit has been missed. The UN Environment Programme's Emissions Gap Report found best-case warming would peak at 1.7 to 1.8 degrees Celsius around mid-century, requiring emissions to fall 45 percent below 2025 levels by 2035 — a cut not on track. Reporter Bob Berwyn argues the overshoot era is an invoice for past underinvestment rather than grounds to skip negotiations, where countries set emission cuts, adaptation and financing each year. Adaptation finance falls short: even tripling it would raise only $85 billion to $120 billion annually against developing nations' estimated need of $305 billion. Reporter Keerti Gopal noted the loss and damage fund's first round covers less than 1 percent of Nepal's losses, underscoring the shortfall Berwyn says must not be spent on less.

visual null
items.title: Climate Delegates Reject Overshoot as Excuse for Inaction

items.summary: US prices rose 0.4% in October, below September's 0.6%, yet still above the 0.3% analysts had expected. The rise was driven by increases in housing, food and energy costs, though energy price rises slowed to 0.7% from 5.2%. Because inflation came in higher than forecast, analysts say it raises the chance of an interest rate increase at the Federal Reserve's December meeting; governor Christopher Waller had already signalled a lean toward raising rates even if October figures were slower. The Bureau of Labor Statistics measured the change through the consumer price index and did not publish a 12-month figure for October after failing to collect data in time, while noting inflation was 3.7% over the year to September.
items.title: US October Inflation Beats Expectations, Raising Fed Rate Hopes

items.summary: The UK government launched a leak inquiry into how Bloomberg reported bank tax details hours before the budget, with Chancellor John Healey to face questions. Separately, higher-than-expected October US inflation pushed stocks lower and raised odds of a December rate hike.
items.title: UK launches leak probe as US inflation jolts Wall Street

items.summary: Gasoline dipped below $4 a gallon Tuesday, per AAA, after falling 38 cents in the last month to $3.98 nationally. Yet consumer prices rose 0.4% in October from the Labor Department, exceeding forecasts, with housing costs driving much of it. Rising diesel and freight costs add pressure as heating oil climbs amid cold weather.
items.title: Gas Prices Fall as Inflation Stays High

items.summary: Greta Thunberg opened Cop31 in Antalya warning that climate change threatens everything and everyone, urging action to protect people rather than sacrifice the global majority for a few. The summit coincides with Turkey announcing two new oilfields and other nations expanding fossil fuel output despite transition pledges.
items.title: Thunberg Warns as Cop31 Opens in Turkey Amid Fossil Fuel Debate

items.summary: Defense secretary Pete Hegseth called Thomas Massie’s articles of impeachment a ‘political spectacle’ and personal ego-driven attack during his Pentagon press conference. The House is poised to vote on whether to refer the resolution for investigation or table it, with possible floor action by Wednesday.
items.title: Hegseth dismisses impeachment as political spectacle

items.summary: French police made arrests after searching three properties, including the Ritz hotel in Paris and Villa Sainte-Thérèse in Saint-Tropez, on 13 and 14 October 2026. The Metropolitan Police confirmed a number of arrests following interviews with several victims. Searches were conducted alongside British investigators as part of an investigation into alleged abuse by Mohamed Al Fayed.
items.title: French Police Arrests in Al Fayed Abuse Probe

items.summary: The Associated Press reports that many defectors view Kim Jong Un's daughter, reportedly about 13 and named Kim Ju Ae, as the likely next leader of North Korea. Since late 2022 she has made dozens of public appearances with her father at weapons tests and military parades; state media calls her 'most beloved' child, and eight of the 11 defectors interviewed by the AP shared that view. Doubts remain rooted in her gender: only one of 17 department directors for the ruling Workers' Party is a woman. Observers nonetheless expect Kim Jong Un to designate a successor who will face little resistance at home, as past successions suggest passive acceptance.
items.title: Defectors See North Korea's Kim Jong Un Daughter as Likely Heir

items.summary: The documentary "The Sea We Call Home" is presented through director's notes that describe its approach rather than report measurable findings. Rather than advancing a predetermined argument, the film centers five personal stories about people who have lived by the South China Sea for generations: an island dweller, fishermen following ancestral routes, reef divers, those adapting to shifting fishing grounds, and residents of Tanmen waiting for boats. The notes explain that disputes appear only as context while restraint guided its telling.
items.title: Director's Notes on The Sea We Call Home

items.summary: CGTN reporters are returning to the people and islands they filmed more than a decade ago, marking their comeback after thirteen years. The series, titled 'The Sea We Call Home,' will premiere on November 11 and explores familiar faces, old memories, and new beginnings that reveal how much has changed in lives and on these home islands.
items.title: CGTN Reporters Return After Thirteen Years for New Documentary

items.summary: Indonesia's vice president, Gibran Rakabuming Raka, offered to resign during a Tuesday meeting with President Prabowo Subianto, according to officials. The talks lasted over two hours and followed mounting questions about his academic credentials after the Supreme Court ruled they did not meet election requirements. It was unclear whether Prabowo accepted the offer.
items.title: Indonesian Vice President Offers Resignation Over Eligibility Questions

items.summary: US inflation rose 0. 4% from September to October, a slight cooldown as gas costs fell during the month, though it edged above expectations. The Bureau of Labor Statistics did not release its usual year-over-year figure because data was not collected in October 2025 amid the government shutdown. Energy prices remained elevated, and inflation has stayed above an annualized 3% since late February. AAA reported gas averaging $4. 41 at month start to $4. 22 by end of October. Fed chair Kevin Warsh said the central bank remains focused on easing price increases while keeping expectations anchored.
items.title: US Inflation Cooled in October as Gas Prices Dipped

items.summary: The average transaction cost for a new vehicle in the U.S. reached a record high of $51,109, according to a report from Kelley Blue Book, part of Cox Automotive. That figure is roughly $500 above the prior December 2025 record and up about 2.1% over the past year — below inflation, Erin Keating noted. The transaction cost includes sticker price, add-ons, minus incentives, but excludes auto-loan interest. Rising production costs from tariffs on steel, aluminum and Canadian goods; higher chip and copper prices; and a shift toward larger vehicles all push prices up. Meanwhile, used cars average close to $27,000, 6% higher than last year.
items.title: U.S. New Car Costs Hit Record $51,109 Average

items.summary: Google DeepMind researchers introduced AlphaProof Code, a framework that used AI agents with human oversight to formally verify the compiled code of Signal's cryptographic protocol. The work claims this is the first time an AI has verified such a widely deployed protocol at implementation depth, and that it completed in four weeks versus years historically.
items.title: Google DeepMind's AlphaProof Code Formally Verifies Signal Protocol Code

items.summary: The film industry faces a dystopian prospect as AI generates stories and recreates screen icons, but its immediate impact already reaches behind-the-scenes jobs. Hollywood figures like James Cameron sit on an AI board; Steven Soderbergh used Meta-powered animation; Christopher Nolan called the idea of replacement “nonsense” yet conceded useful imaging tools arise. The clearest target is the storyboard artist: Martin Scorsese partnered with an AI firm in June for storyboarding his next film, and even Bong Joon Ho likens shooting without them to standing in Grand Central Terminal wearing only underwear. Artists stress that boards are collaborative art, not just drawings; Ferdinando Cocco notes a return to analogue practice and sees communication forcing creative expansion. Alex Clark predicts greater appreciation for films with a human touch as AI grows.
items.title: Film Artists Warn AI Threatens Storyboard Craft

items.summary: Researchers at the University of Pretoria’s Institute for Sustainable Malaria Control argue that scientific progress against malaria is not turning into effective action. They identify three obstacles: prediction versus preparedness, evidence versus implementation, and awareness versus behaviour. Although sub-Saharan Africa accounts for around 95% of global cases, early-warning systems such as Ethiopia’s in Bahir Dar have shown detection can inform planning. A study involving more than 7,500 people found that while most recognised symptoms, bed net use remained low due to cost and access. The World Health Organization reported in April 2025 that more than 40% of planned insecticide-treated net campaigns were delayed or at risk. Closing the gap requires strengthening health systems, improving community access, and coordinating across borders, particularly in southern Africa where malaria crosses national lines.
items.title: Three Barriers Blocking Malaria Science Into Action in Africa

items.summary: A PhD student in economics and behavioural researcher Sophia Seelos tracked two decades of crop cycles and protests in Kenya, combining satellite-measured plant greenness with the Armed Conflict Location Events Dataset (ACLED) for 2000 to 2019. They found that approximately 7% of all protests over this period related to agrarian conditions, and that unrest increased two to three months after harvest, peaking around sowing as households faced financial stress during the lean season. The authors suggest governments, donors and social protection programmes could anticipate these periods using local agricultural calendars.
items.title: Kenyan Agrarian Protests Follow a Seasonal Pattern

items.summary: A study published on 24 September in IEEE Transactions on Applied Superconductivity outlines CERN's work manufacturing next-generation magnets for the Large Hadron Collider. The current collider uses niobium-titanium coils reaching about 8.3 tesla, roughly 166,000 times Earth's magnetic field. Scientists are developing niobium-tin (Nb₃Sn) coils yielding just under 12 T using a wind-and-react process. Magnet engineer Susana Izquierdo Bermúdez leads a team of about 60 people who produced 250 coils, with 25 failing quality control tests. The High-Luminosity LHC aims for between 140 and 200 particle collisions per experiment after 2030, requiring these compact magnets to observe rare phenomena.
items.title: CERN Engineers Next-Generation Magnets for High-Luminosity LHC

items.summary: Kirt McMaster, CEO and cofounder of a startup building the Linux-based desktop operating system Kora, says it targets “the AI native, not mass market.” Announced Tuesday, Kora aims to integrate context across multiple AI tools at the system level rather than siloing them into apps or browser tabs. It is scheduled to launch sometime in 2027 and runs on Qualcomm Snapdragon PCs next year as well as x86-64 hardware. The company’s team of under 100 people optimizes Kora for desktops with at least 64 gigabytes of RAM, which it says doubles the capacity of Googlebook OS.
items.title: Kirt McMaster Positions AI-Focused Kora OS for Creators

items.summary: The European Union's ENISA agency says artificial intelligence is reshaping cybersecurity, shrinking the time between a vulnerability being discovered and weaponised to near zero while acting as a force multiplier for both attackers and defenders. In its latest report it notes that 57.3% of cyber incidents in 2025 were ideologically driven by geopolitical events such as Russia's war against Ukraine and Middle East conflicts, with most having limited impact; another 29.3% were financially motivated, ransomware remaining the most impactful type on businesses. A cited 2025 NIS Investment study found that 45% of surveyed organisations struggled to find cybersecurity-skilled staff. ENISA urges member states to expand activities and amplify EU programmes in the field.
items.title: ENISA Warns AI Is Speeding Up and Industrialising Cyberattacks

items.summary: A newborn Kalkanovatos ray took its first swim minutes after hatching at an aquarium near the Sani hotel on Greece's Kassandra peninsula, then was released into the Thermaic Gulf. The release is part of the five-year-old Thermaikos Biodiversity Project, which coordinates with the Lamna Institute in Valencia and iSea to rescue rays accidentally caught in fishing nets whose eggs may be expelled under stress. Two pups have already hatched and been returned this year.
items.title: Newborn Kalkanovatos Ray Released After Hatching in Greece Aquarium

items.summary: As the United States, China and Russia prepare to meet at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen on November 18-19, Japan is watching for changes in Washington's approach to the Indo-Pacific. Tokyo fears that President Donald Trump may seek a diplomatic quick win after his midterm-election losses, one that could overlook its allies' interests. Experts say he might treat Taiwan as leverage or ignore rare-earth export restrictions China placed on Japan. Analysts also warn about US outreach toward Russia and North Korea. Rather than rely solely on the alliance, Tokyo has diversified security partnerships with European Union states, NATO, Australia and others while reaffirming its commitment to preserving regional stability.
items.title: Japan watches Trump's foreign policy before APEC

items.summary: NVIDIA introduced Snapshot, an open-source checkpoint and restore system for GPU workloads on Kubernetes as part of the DSX AI Factory Platform. It captures fully initialized CPU and GPU memory so replicas can resume in seconds instead of minutes during cold starts. Design partners reported large gains: Crusoe cut GLM Pod readiness from roughly 8 minutes to 31 seconds, and Saturn Cloud reduced vLLM startup from 2–8.5 minutes to 6–34 seconds on NVIDIA HGX B300 hardware. Across tested configurations Snapshot restored replicas under 45 seconds—8x to 36x faster than cold start—and checkpoint plus restore was shorter than a single cold start in every case.
items.title: NVIDIA Snapshot Cuts GPU Workload Startup Times

items.summary: NVIDIA announced two open source projects in public preview, NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine (NVKE) and NVIDIA Kubernetes Recipes (NVKR), which together build and operate managed Kubernetes services on GPU infrastructure. NVKE provides software to run a managed service with APIs for provisioning clusters, while NVKR builds reproducible node images from version-pinned sources. Both are Apache 2.0 licensed components of the DSX AI Factory Platform. The projects remain in public preview, may change between releases, and are not yet recommended for production workloads. NVIDIA Cloud Partners Firmus and SK Telecom, plus partners Mirantis, Rafay, Spectro Cloud, OpenNebula Systems, and vCluster, are integrating them into their offerings.
items.title: NVIDIA Announces Open Source Kubernetes Engine for GPU Infrastructure

items.summary: Meta introduced Your algorithm, an end-to-end suite of AI-powered tools that makes Facebook recommendations more transparent and steerable through a single editable view. The system lets users state interests in their own words across Feed and Reels via Interested In and Not Interested In lists, with changes applied responsively at every stage from profile generation to LLM reranking and device-level cache invalidation. Meta describes it as creating a more personalized experience informed by both behavior and stated intent, while noting remaining opportunities such as better interpreting ambiguous input and exploring additional entry points for shaping preferences.
items.title: Meta Unveils Your Algorithm for Personalized, Transparent Recommendations

items.summary: At KubeCon + CloudNativeCon, NVIDIA is deepening its open source commitment by donating the autonomous-agent security runtime OpenShell to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) as a Sandbox project. It also contributes to Agent Substrate, a Google-led framework for scaling agent workloads on Kubernetes, and announces new DSX AI Factory Platform components: NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine and Recipes in public preview, plus NVIDIA Snapshot for faster inference startup. Linux Foundation CEO Jim Zemlin noted the community now faces secure environments for agents. Design partners reported reduced readiness times—Crusoe cut GLM-5.3 from about eight minutes to 31 seconds; Saturn Cloud lowered vLLM startup between two and 8.5 minutes to six and 34 seconds. NVIDIA frames these moves as advancing Kubernetes as the leading foundation for AI workloads at scale.
items.title: NVIDIA Donates OpenShell and Expands Kubernetes AI Offerings at KubeCon

items.summary: Google unveiled two new variants of its tensor processing units (TPUs), the TPU 8tx, developed with AMD, and the TPU 8i Max. The company said in a blog post that these chips broaden its portfolio to confidential inference and greater memory capacity for large workloads, aiming to reduce reliance on externally made chips for cloud computing. Google noted the launch arrives as hyperscalers like Microsoft, Amazon, OpenAI and Anthropic develop their own semiconductors amid Nvidia’s dominance; reports also cited Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitting an affair with someone alleged to be a Chinese spy.
items.title: Google Unveils Two New AI Chips for Confidential Inference and Larger Workloads

items.summary: An alleged espionage scandal involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has intensified scrutiny of the company amid the ongoing technology war between Washington and Beijing. The controversy centers on Alice Huang, a former executive of Singapore-based Megaspeed, under investigation for suspected diversion of advanced Nvidia chips to China. While US intelligence assessments raise unproven concerns about her links to Chinese intelligence, Nvidia's board launched an independent probe and denies any compromise of its secrets or national security. Data from research firm IDC shows Nvidia held 34% of China's data-centre AI chip market in the first half of 2026, shipping about 678,000 accelerators versus Huawei's 572,000 (28%). Reports place Megaspeed's purchases at about $4.8 billion over two years. The dispute reflects broader tensions: US export restrictions since October 2022 aim to limit China's access to advanced computing power, while Congress pushes for stronger oversight through proposals like the AI Overwatch Act and Chip Security Act.
items.title: Nvidia Caught Between US Export Rules and China's AI Demand Amid Espionage Probe

items.summary: Hugging Face now lets organizations link their Hugging Face account to a Google Cloud billing account, so usage appears on the existing Google Cloud invoice instead of requiring a separate credit card. The change is available through the Google Cloud Marketplace and covers Team or Enterprise subscriptions plus pay-as-you-go compute and storage. Until an organization's subscription is approved by the Hugging Face team, any paid usage continues to be billed through its current payment method.
items.title: Hugging Face Adds Google Cloud Billing Option for Organizations

items.summary: Google announced that Gemini 4 Carbon is now available, positioning it as its strongest model with frontier cybersecurity capabilities and long-horizon agentic workflows across software engineering and scientific reasoning. The company says Carbon ranks #1 on CursorBench 4. 0, Perplexity’s WANDR and Zapier’s AutomationBench at more than 2X lower cost per task compared to the next best external model, though it pairs frontier accuracy with practical production economics. It is available via API in Google AI Studio and Gemini for business at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens — the same introductory price as Argon — and is rolling out to Ultra subscribers across Antigravity, the app and Search. In simulated cyberattack testing environments seeded with ExploitBench and CyScenarioBench, Carbon blocked 99% of attack trajectories from Google’s adaptive red-teaming agent (down from 3. 1% on Argon), lowering the per-attempt breach rate to just 0. 8%.
items.title: Google Makes Gemini 4 Carbon Available

items.summary: Anthropic is pursuing a stock market flotation valuing the company at up to $1.4tn (£1.05tn), below the $2tn previously expected, after investors questioned AI-boom durability following midterm election wins for datacentre opponents. A US regulatory filing on Tuesday reported the lower target; trading could begin next week. The company plans to raise up to $64.4bn by selling 825m shares at up to $78 each, with a further $26bn via private placement involving Alphabet and Nvidia.
items.title: Anthropic Sets $1.4tn Valuation Ahead of IPO

items.summary: On Nov. 10, Anthropic announced it was bringing its Claude assistant into video conferencing platform Google Meet as part of a wider effort to embed AI in office work. The feature, called Claude Meetings, lets users add Claude to calls so it can follow discussions and turn them into tasks, timelines and answers live. It launches in beta for Team and Enterprise customers through Google Meet before expanding elsewhere.
items.title: Anthropic Adds Claude Assistant to Google Meet for Live Meeting Tasks

items.summary: On Tuesday, IBM announced it was ending US visa and green card sponsorship for a majority of roles in IBM Consulting, which employs more than 150,000 people. The decision follows heightened scrutiny of foreign tech hiring under Donald Trump's administration, which last month suspended several companies from the Permanent Labor Certification process. A company spokesperson said participation in high-skilled visa programs has declined over years as skill availability and client needs have evolved.
items.title: IBM Ends Visa and Green Card Sponsorship for Most Consulting Roles

items.summary: At Web Summit in Lisbon, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted on stage that he had an affair with a Chinese datacenter executive suspected to be a Beijing spy. The disclosure sent Nvidia shares down 7.5% at the open, wiping over $330bn off its value. Cloudflare's Matthew Prince framed the episode as a threat to Nvidia's market dominance and questioned whether its financing practices were legitimate financial engineering. Huang apologized in an employee letter; his board launched an independent investigation into national security concerns. The article also examines Silicon Valley tech leaders attempting reconciliation with newly elected Democrats after last month's elections.
items.title: Nvidia CEO affair and tech's political reckoning

items.summary: President Trump defended Nvidia chief Jensen Huang, saying he believes Huang's explanation that he was unaware of former executive Alice Huang's alleged intelligence connections and expected the FBI probe not to damage his position. The defence follows allegations that roughly 240,000 advanced processors were moved into China through intermediaries in a network worth $7.5 billion, which Reuters said it had not independently verified. Nvidia launched an independent board investigation while shareholders filed a proposed class-action lawsuit; shares fell 4.27% to $178.67 Monday and later opened 2.09% higher at $182.40 Tuesday. Lawmakers from both parties pressed for answers, and China dismissed the reports as groundless speculation.
items.title: Trump Defends Nvidia Chief Amid China Allegations

items.summary: Google DeepMind released Gemini Robotics 2.5, a robotic AI platform it says is approaching human-level performance on real-world tasks. The version scored a 30 to 100 percent higher success rate and was 20 to 30 percent faster than the prior release in laboratory tests across more than 200 activities. Powered by Gemini Robotics 2.5, Apptronik’s Apollo 2 robots tied bows and reached a 96 percent success rate kitting parts at Mercedes-Benz factories in Europe. DeepMind director Kanishka Rao called closing the remaining gap to human performance “a steep road.”
items.title: DeepMind Unveils Gemini Robotics 2.5 With Safety Benchmark

items.summary: The Supreme Court, in a suo motu case titled ‘In Re: Victims of Digital Arrest Related to Forged Documents’, directed WhatsApp and other intermediaries to submit proposed measures against digital arrest scams and related cybercrimes. A bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant listed the plea for further consideration on November 23. The court emphasised that financial institutions must compensate victims where fraud results from a bank's failure to exercise due diligence, noting cyber crimes fell 50 per cent this year yet victims lost Rs 800 crore so far. Banks were described as a protective umbrella with transaction data they should use to prevent fraud before money leaves an account. The bench also directed the RBI and state law enforcement agencies to submit reports and suggestions for prevention and prosecution, and listed the plea for further hearing on November 23.
items.title: Supreme Court Orders Intermediaries and Banks on Digital Arrest Scam Prevention

items.summary: Anthropic announced new workplace features on Tuesday, including Claude Meetings, which adds the assistant to video calls so it can draft plans while participants talk. The company also unveiled Claude Whiteboards and Claude Sheets for real-time collaboration. These launches follow similar tools from OpenAI and Meta as AI vendors compete with Microsoft and Google over office suites.
items.title: Anthropic Launches Claude Meetings and Other Workplace Tools in Beta

items.summary: The USDA Foreign Agricultural Service office in New Delhi forecasts Indian apple imports to rise about 19 per cent to 5.11 lakh tonnes during the 2026-27 marketing year, driven by rising domestic consumption and stronger demand for high-quality fruit. Consumption is seen growing roughly 5 per cent from a revised 2.76 million tonnes in 2025-26. The outlook follows cautious procurement amid supply volatility; production is expected to grow about 3 per cent at 2.59 million tonnes, supported by favourable conditions in Jammu and Kashmir after weaker yields elsewhere.
items.title: USDA Forecasts Sharp Rise in India's Apple Imports for 2026-27

items.summary: Kunal Shah, WhatsApp's global head since June 2026, outlined three priorities on Tuesday: more expressive conversations, simpler financial and everyday transactions, and AI to help users complete tasks. He said his first four months focused on understanding what the platform's over three billion users want.
items.title: WhatsApp chief Kunal Shah reveals platform priorities

items.summary: CPCA data shows Tesla wholesaled only 8,817 cars in China from Giga Shanghai in October, the lowest domestic level since July 2022. Of 67,829 vehicles built that month, 59,012 were exports, leaving just 8,817 for Chinese buyers—down 66% year-over-year and 86% from September's 64,837. Analysts note Tesla front-loads export orders early in each quarter while pushing domestic deliveries later; October is the first month of a new quarter. Still, Electrek argues the cycle alone cannot explain why this October was less than half any other this year or one-third of last October's 26,006 low. Through October, China sales fell 15% to 389,905 cars while Giga Shanghai exports rose 101% to 420,984—more abroad than at home for the first time. Beijing plans to cut EV export VAT rebates from 13% to 9% on April 1, 2027, which may pressure automakers to front-load shipments further.
items.title: Tesla China Domestic Sales Collapse as Exports Surge

items.summary: A 60-year-old Danish man, Klaus Elmfelt Aerenlund, filed a lawsuit in San Francisco County Superior Court against OpenAI after following legal advice from ChatGPT. He claims the chatbot told him he could stop paying rent during his dog dispute with his landlord and that losing his home was legally impossible. After three months without payment, he was evicted in June 2026 and lived in his car before finding temporary shelter at a campsite.
items.title: Danish Man Sues OpenAI After ChatGPT Rent Advice Led To Eviction

items.summary: At Lisbon's Web Summit, allegations of Chinese spying on Nvidia overshadowed proceedings. Nvidia shares fell more than five percent in Tuesday afternoon Wall Street trading. Jensen Huang acknowledged an affair with a woman US intelligence suspects spies for China, though Beijing denied the claim. Executives see opportunities amid turmoil; Larry Li noted short-term stock turbulence but possible benefits for rivals like Qualcomm and AMD.
items.title: Nvidia Scandal Dominates Web Summit as Shares Fall and Rivals Eye Gains

items.summary: Columnist Liz asks how a CEO who delivered 700,000% returns could be removed, noting President Donald Trump believes Jensen Huang should keep his job. Prediction markets currently price about 14% odds of firing by year's end, though the author hedges that Nvidia shares may recover within weeks. The board runs its own investigation into who knew what and when.
items.title: Trump backs Jensen Huang amid Nvidia spy scandal

items.summary: Apple released twelve software updates on Tuesday, patching wireless security flaws in Bluetooth pairing, AirPlay connection rate limits, and Messages across iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, and VisionOS. Apple’s notes say the fixes address issues like unauthorized group-chat joins and PIN brute-forcing; some vulnerabilities were found internally while others came from researchers. Reports link two of them to earlier studies by French researchers and Oligo.
items.title: Apple Ships Twelve Security Patches for Wireless Flaws Across Its Devices

items.summary: On Diwali night Delhi's PM2.5 hit 3,744 micrograms per cubic metre in Mundka, with 125 CPCB readings missing and official AQI questioned; NASA satellite captured haze over northern India while a Yamuna river safari began.
items.title: Delhi pollution tops 3,744 as Nvidia chief faces spy probe

items.summary: Researchers at Google DeepMind used an AI system called AlphaProof Code, built on the Gemini Carbon model, to formally verify portions of Signal’s underlying cryptographic code. The work mathematically proved that parts of the encrypted messaging app’s code function as intended without errors — a task completed in about a month that might normally take experts years. It builds on earlier verification by the Signal Foundation and is open-sourced; DeepMind did not release it as a consumer product, though WhatsApp and Google Messages use similar encryption.
items.title: Google DeepMind uses AI to verify Signal encryption

items.summary: A controversy involving Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang has drawn scrutiny from US authorities, an FBI investigation and a shareholder lawsuit. Reports allege that connections linked to Alice Huang helped route roughly $7.5 billion in AI-chip shipments to Chinese customers, potentially implicating export controls. The New York Times reported the intelligence allegations; Reuters reviewed shipping records showing Megaspeed International's Indonesian subsidiary imported Nvidia processors between 2024 and 2026. Nvidia's board launched an independent investigation on November 8 and stated it had no reason to believe trade secrets or national security interests were compromised, while China rejected the espionage claims as unsubstantiated. Nvidia shares fell 4.3% to $178.67 on November 9, reducing its market capitalisation by about $190 billion. The article notes that none of these allegations establish wrongdoing and that questions remain under investigation.
items.title: Nvidia and Jensen Huang face probe over alleged China intelligence links

items.summary: Jensen Huang admitted an extramarital affair with a suspected Chinese spy, which the author says threatens to inject uncertainty into the AI ecosystem. The piece argues that CEO scandals signal deeper governance risks and succession problems. Nvidia has no clear heir apparent for Huang, who wants decades in his role, and Bloomberg News reported he built an informal structure around himself. The board's early statement on its investigation sounds premature; because Nvidia is a multi-trillion-dollar company centered on one person, any threat to Huang risks the whole enterprise.
items.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang Affair Raises Succession Fears

items.summary: An analysis of the Nvidia affair examines how Jensen Huang's reported relationship with Alice Huang, suspected by US intelligence of ties to China, raises concerns about protecting strategically important technology firms from foreign interference. While China denies espionage allegations, Nvidia launched an independent investigation stating no reason to believe sensitive information was compromised.
items.title: Nvidia Affair Raises Questions on AI Security and Succession Planning

items.summary: Amazon Connect Customer introduced Mitra-v2, the second generation of a tabular foundation model pretrained on synthetic tables. Unlike earlier tools that require per-table setup, one pretrained model reads labeled rows from an unseen table and predicts the rest via in-context learning. The architecture is unchanged; pretraining now uses tables with 10 times as many rows and roughly three times as many columns as Mitra-v1, plus a new hybrid synthetic prior. On TabArena, a public benchmark of 51 real-world datasets maintained by an independent academic team, Mitra-v2 leads the single-model field, outperforming Mitra-v1 on 32 of 33 shared datasets and completing all 51 within one hour. It also ranks first among fine-tuned models on ScoringBench for regression.
items.title: Amazon Connect Customer launches Mitra-v2 tabular foundation model

items.summary: The New York Fed's Center for Microeconomic Data reports that credit card delinquency rose sharply between 2022 and 2024, with the steepest increases among borrowers in lower-income neighborhoods. The analysis accompanies the latest Quarterly Report on Household Debt and Credit, which shows total nominal household debt balances increased by $334 billion in Q3 2026, a 1.8 percent rise from Q2 2026. During the pandemic, new cards went increasingly to lower-income borrowers with weaker credit scores; those accounts now show higher distress as forbearances and stimulus faded.
items.title: New York Fed Finds Credit Card Delinquency Widening by Income After 2022

items.summary: President Donald Trump said the FBI is investigating Nvidia's chief executive over an alleged affair with a person tied to Chinese intelligence, widening fallout from the scandal around the world's largest chipmaker. Shares fell after Jensen Huang admitted infidelity with an executive linked to Chinese intelligence. Lawmakers in a soon-to-be Democrat-controlled Congress have pledged investigations, and the Commerce Department has reportedly begun preparing new semiconductor export controls.
items.title: Trump Says FBI Investigating Nvidia CEO Over Alleged Chinese Spy Link

items.summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, the same underlying model offered at two safeguard levels. Fable adds classifiers that block high-risk cybersecurity tasks and most research biology so it can reach all users; Mythos drops those blocks but requires membership in Anthropic's Cyber Verification Program and Life Sciences Verification Program. When Fable blocks a query, users receive an answer from Opus 4.8 (cyber) or Opus 5 (biology). All benchmark scores are self-reported by Anthropic and not independently verified; for example, Fable scored 64.9% on RoboDojo Sim versus GPT-6 Astra's 29.8%, while AutomationBench showed Gemini 4 Carbon ahead at 53.9% to Fable's 51.4%. Pricing starts at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, with a fast mode priced higher.
items.title: Anthropic Ships Claude Fable and Mythos 5.2 With Different Safeguards

items.summary: The Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics reported on Nov 10 that the Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% in October after advancing 0.6% in September, below economists polled by Reuters who had expected a 0.3% gain. Core CPI climbed 0.3%, matching forecasts. The article notes inflation remains above the Fed's 2% target and left markets pricing a December rate increase.
items.title: US October CPI rises above forecast, Fed set for December rate hike

items.summary: Jensen Huang, chief executive and co-founder of Nvidia, admitted an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, who has been accused of being a Chinese intelligence agent. Nvidia is the world's largest supplier of high-end AI chips, with some estimates placing its market share over 80%. Sales of its most powerful chips to China have been restricted since 2022, though relaxed last year. Trade records indicate over US$3 billion in chips crossed from Singapore to China in a single year. Nvidia's share price fell after the disclosure, and it is reportedly under criminal investigation while Congress requests Huang explain his interactions with Alice Huang.
items.title: Nvidia Scandal and AI Chip Fallout

items.summary: Anthropic released its Economic Index report, which identifies six patterns in how people use the AI tool Claude, from tax-day rushes to weekend chats. The findings show that personal conversations make up about 35% on weekdays and nearly 50% on weekends; at 6 p.m., recipe requests occur at 2.3 times the average rate; and before the April 14 filing deadline, tax questions reached eight times their usual May share. Work output differs by context: documents appear in 20% of work conversations versus explanations at 17%. Higher-paid workers consume 2.07 times more tokens than lower-paid ones. Michael S. Barr notes little evidence that AI displaces jobs. Anthropic's researchers suggest automation may be labor-augmenting, while Federal Reserve Board economists Leland D. Crane and Paul E. Soto find coder employment growth about 3 percent lower since ChatGPT arrived. Managers over-represent the survey respondents at 23% versus 7% of U.S. employment, which could skew optimism among heavy users.
items.title: Anthropic's Economic Index Reveals Six Patterns in Claude Use

items.summary: On the Monday after Nvidia's board announced an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang, Nvidia stock fell as much as 8 per cent before recovering to about 4 per cent below Friday's close. The probe examined allegations that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation involving a woman suspected of working for China. For three years Nvidia had been the engine of US stocks' rise; analysts now warn the bigger risk may be tighter chip restrictions on China ahead of its November 17 results.
items.title: Nvidia Stock Slides on CEO Probe While Wall Street Rallies

items.summary: The Singapore Food Agency, via Senior Director Cheong Lai Peng, responds to Liu Fook Thim's letter calling for affordable local vegetables at shopping venues. The agency notes that while local farms support food resilience and supply buffers, they face higher land and manpower costs than imported alternatives. SFA is working with the Singapore Agro-Food Enterprises Federation on productivity gains, technology adoption, aggregation, and new sales channels to improve price competitiveness.
items.title: SFA Commits to Affordable Local Produce

items.summary: The Ministry of Transport responded to a letter questioning new financing restrictions on individually owned private-hire cars that took effect Oct 30, 2026. The rules treat such vehicles like other privately owned cars because they serve both personal and hire purposes. Changes aim for consistent treatment while preventing over-leveraging. The ministry will monitor arrangements including in-house loans and long-term leasing against the 100% business loans.
items.title: MOT Clarifies Financing Rules for Individually Owned Private-Hire Cars

items.summary: Three contract workers died on 9 November 2026 while cleaning a wastewater treatment tank during maintenance at a Tata Electronics factory near Hosur, Tamil Nadu. They collapsed after reportedly inhaling toxic fumes and were declared dead on arrival at a hospital in Hosur. The facility supplies casings for Apple iPhones. B. Akmal (28), M. Sarathi Kumar (28) from Dharmapuri, and Kaveri (30) of Hosur were among the victims. Minister S Keerthana said the incident would be thoroughly investigated.
items.title: Three Workers Die Cleaning Tank at Tata Electronics iPhone Parts Factory

items.summary: GitHub rewrote the software engine behind several Copilot products, porting its codebase from TypeScript to Rust using GitHub Copilot itself. The effort was triggered by heavy resource use and difficulty embedding Copilot elsewhere; a full rewrite would have needed many developers over about two years. Using the Copilot app, CLI, and AI agents, one developer finished it in a few months. An early estimate put porting at roughly 130K lines, but more logic moved out of the interface layer, so ultimately around 430K lines were migrated. The rewrite cut client lifecycle time from about 5.25 seconds to 292 milliseconds and raised throughput from 7.55 to 120 completed session lifecycles per second; in a 10-client test peak private memory fell from roughly 1383 MB to 126 MB.
items.title: GitHub Rewrote Copilot’s Engine in Months With AI

items.summary: The Central Pollution Control Board defended its air quality monitoring methodology, explaining why official AQI readings are capped at 500 despite private apps reporting levels as high as 1,800 in Delhi after Diwali. The board said the ceiling is an intentional feature of the National Air Quality Index (NAQI), consistent with international practices including US EPA scale, since all such levels fall under the 'Severe' category and do not change health advisories.
items.title: CPCB Defends Capping Official Air Quality Index at 500

items.summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat defended traditional Diwali practices, stating earlier firecrackers were free of harmful chemicals and helped eliminate insects while purifying the air. His comments arrive as air quality worsens across Delhi and other metropolitan cities, where fireworks remain a contentious issue over their environmental and health impacts.
items.title: RSS Chief Defends Traditional Diwali Firecrackers Amid Delhi Pollution Crisis

items.summary: TypeSafe AI introduced Jev, a decision model that returns structured decisions and probabilities instead of generating text token by token. Hugging Face now supports the interface through transformers classes and llama.cpp, aiming to agree on a common contract without forcing one implementation.
items.title: Hugging Face Introduces Decision Models for LLMs

items.summary: In an episode of Leaders Talk, CMG's Zou Yun spoke with Alexander De Croo, administrator of the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), about China's development achievements and its role in advancing global sustainable development. They explored how the CIIE can create new opportunities for international cooperation and examined how China's commitment to high-standard opening-up may benefit the world.
items.title: UNDP Administrator Discusses China's Role in Global Development

items.summary: A CGTN opinion piece by Liu Chunsheng argues that China's October consumer price index rise of 0.7% year-on-year and core CPI gain of 0.8%, both easing, reflect a K-shaped split rather than broad demand recovery. He notes the headline is driven mainly by energy and AI-related electronics, while food prices keep falling and industrial goods stay flat. The producer price index rose 5.7% in October as profits of large industrial firms grew 15.5% over nine months against retail sales rising just 1.1%. Core CPI staying below 1% shows demand-driven recovery has not yet appeared, so the author calls for raising household incomes and expanding domestic demand rather than relying on rate cuts alone.
items.title: China's CPI recovery masks price divergence, commentator says

items.summary: Journalist Mona Chalabi, in her book Ten Lives, describes financial insecurity felt across the U.S. economic spectrum after profiling 10 Americans over five years. She says nearly everyone she interviewed expressed a sense of panic about their finances, which she links to what she calls an especially precarious American system. Chalabi also notes that many profiled people identified as middle class regardless of actual income and considered parental wealth central to their own economic security. The piece is drawn from interview highlights covering partner selection trends and her transparency about compensation.
items.title: Author Frames Widespread Financial Anxiety as American 'Panic',

items.summary: Sources briefed on UK government proposals say a substantial expansion of the under-16s social media ban, set to come into force in March, could inadvertently extend coverage to platforms such as YouTube Kids, Lego Play, Spotify and games services. One source close to the talks said up to 150 platforms may now be covered. The regulations are expected for cabinet signoff this week, with culture secretary Lisa Nandy due to lay them in parliament in December. Tech companies argue that removing recommender systems would make their sites non-functional, prompting calls for clearer guidelines.
items.title: UK social media ban expansion could cover YouTube Kids and other sites

items.summary: Carbon Brief analysis of provisional UNFCCC lists shows more than 92,000 people registered for COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, potentially the largest COP ever. Party delegates number 18,812; including overflow raises that to over 34,000. Host nation Turkey sent 2,950 people, ahead of Brazil (1,994), Nigeria and China. The UNFCCC will release final figures after the summit.
items.title: COP31 registration tops previous summits as host nation leads delegate counts

items.summary: On Tuesday, Kemi Badenoch and Helen Whately held a press conference in Westminster explaining plans to cut £36.1bn from the welfare budget, with up to £10,000 per household removed. The article frames the announcement as an opposition party re-announcing figures previously discussed at the Conservative party conference last month, noting such costings are rarely taken seriously and may fail before Christmas. Whately presented the numbers while dismissing charities’ warnings of a surge in child poverty and acknowledging only limited compassion for terminally ill or retired claimants. The piece satirises the government’s approach without independent verification of its economic claims.
items.title: Badenoch and Whately Outline Welfare Budget Cuts

items.summary: Israel's newly sworn-in parliament has begun competing over who will form the next government, with opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot tasked by President Isaac Herzog after receiving more Knesset recommendations than outgoing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Both blocs fell short of a majority in the 120-seat body: Eisenkot's four parties won 48 seats and Netanyahu's won 53. Eisenkot has 28 days, with a possible two-week extension, to build a coalition. Arab-led alliances gained an unprecedented 19 seats between them, potentially holding the balance of power, while ultra-Orthodox parties oppose conscription reforms central to Eisenkot's four principles. Netanyahu and Eisenkot exchanged sharp warnings about governing across ideological lines as uncertainty over the outcome grows.
items.title: Eisenkot Tasked With Forming Government After New Knesset Swearing-In

items.summary: A reporter travels with a Ukrainian drone unit called Peaky Blinders into the heavily bombed city of Slovyansk, in eastern Ukraine's Donetsk region. The team escorts them through constant bombardment from Russian drones and glide bombs, past rubble and abandoned vehicles destroyed by remotely operated drones. Slovyansk is one of four cities forming Ukraine's 'fortress belt', central to resumed peace talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US after nine months, which Ukrainian officials say Kyiv refuses to cede territory over. The unit's commander Oleksandr rejects Russia's claim that seizing the Donbas will end the war, while resident Alina Shyrko coordinates civilian evacuations as families leave amid deteriorating conditions.
items.title: Ukraine's drone unit holds devastated Slovyansk amid evacuation

items.summary: The Senate voted Monday, the article states, to advance bipartisan permitting legislation known as BAAJA of 2026. The vote tally was reported as 73-25.
